objectives: By the end of the week, students will use ratios to represent and solve constant-speed situations, compare situations by examining ratios, and organize equivalent ratios in tables. Students will explain how corresponding values are related and use tables, double number lines, and unit rates to support their reasoning. Students will also complete a lighter DeltaMath assignment and submit missing work before grades are finalized on November 20.
agenda:
Monday, November 16: Lesson 9 – Constant Speed
Use ratios and double number line diagrams to represent distance and time at a constant speed. Find missing values and explain how equivalent ratios describe the same speed.
Cool-down: Solve a constant-speed problem and justify the corresponding distance and time values.

Tuesday, November 17: Lesson 10 – Comparing Situations by Examining Ratios
Compare two situations by examining their ratios, unit rates, tables, or double number line diagrams. Determine which situation has the greater rate and explain the comparison in context.
Cool-down: Compare two ratio situations and support the conclusion with mathematical evidence.

Wednesday, November 18: Lesson 11 – Representing Ratios with Tables
Organize equivalent ratios in tables and use multiplication or division to find missing values. Explain how each row represents the same ratio relationship.
Cool-down: Complete a ratio table and explain how the values in each row are related.

Thursday, November 19: Independent DeltaMath and Grade Catch-Up
Mr. Chen is out today. Complete this week's lighter DeltaMath assignment, review unfinished classwork, and submit missing assignments that can still be counted toward your grade. Work quietly, show your calculations, and ask the covering teacher for help with directions when needed.

Friday, November 20: Final Catch-Up Day – Grades Due
Mr. Chen is out today. Finish and submit the lighter DeltaMath assignment and any remaining eligible missing work. Check that your name and homeroom are on every paper. Grades are due today, so use the class period responsibly and turn in completed work before the end of class.
homework: Complete the lighter DeltaMath assignment and submit eligible missing work by Friday, November 20. Review your notes from Lessons 9–11 and correct cool-down responses when requested. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will describe constant-speed relationships using the terms distance, time, speed, ratio, and equivalent.
Students will compare ratio situations using unit rate, greater than, less than, and mathematical evidence.
Students will explain how the rows and columns of a ratio table represent corresponding quantities and equivalent ratios.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will represent and solve equivalent-ratio problems using double number line diagrams, determine unit rates by finding how much for one, and use ratios to reason about constant-speed situations. Students will explain how corresponding values are related and complete a cool-down after each instructional lesson to demonstrate individual understanding.
agenda:
Monday, November 9: Lesson 6 – Introducing Double Number Line Diagrams
Represent multiple batches and equivalent ratios on double number line diagrams. Interpret aligned values and connect each pair of corresponding values to the same ratio relationship.
Cool-down: Complete and interpret a double number line for a given ratio.

Tuesday, November 10: Lesson 7 – Creating Double Number Line Diagrams
Create and label double number line diagrams to represent equivalent ratios and solve problems. Choose useful intervals and explain how the values on the two number lines correspond.
Cool-down: Construct a double number line and use it to answer an equivalent-ratio question.
Wednesday, November 11: No School – Veterans Day

Thursday, November 12: Lesson 8 – How Much for One?
Use division and double number line diagrams to determine the amount associated with one unit. Compare strategies for finding a unit rate and explain what the value means in context.
Cool-down: Find and interpret how much for one in a ratio situation.

Friday, November 13: Lesson 9 – Constant Speed
Use ratios and double number line diagrams to represent distance and time at a constant speed. Find missing values and explain how equivalent ratios describe the same speed.
Cool-down: Solve a constant-speed problem and justify the corresponding distance and time values.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath or lesson practice on equivalent ratios, double number line diagrams, unit rates, and constant speed. Review and correct cool-down responses when requested. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will describe corresponding values on a double number line using the terms ratio, equivalent, scale, and interval.
Students will explain the meaning of a unit rate using the phrases for one and per one in the context of a problem.
Students will justify constant-speed solutions using distance, time, speed, and equivalent-ratio language.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will recognize and generate equivalent ratios in recipes and color mixtures, explain how scaling both quantities by the same factor preserves a ratio, and represent equivalent ratios with double number line diagrams. Each lesson will conclude with a cool-down so students can demonstrate individual understanding and the teacher can use the results to plan the next lesson.
agenda:
Monday, November 2: Lesson 3 – Recipes
Compare recipes and mixtures to determine whether they have the same ratio. Use diagrams and multiple batches to explain why some mixtures taste the same and others taste different.
Cool-down: Independently compare recipe ratios and justify whether the mixtures are equivalent.

Tuesday, November 3: Lesson 4 – Color Mixtures
Use color mixtures to investigate equivalent ratios. Scale both quantities together to create the same shade and explain why changing only one quantity produces a different shade.
Cool-down: Determine whether two color mixtures are equivalent and explain the reasoning.

Wednesday, November 4: Lesson 5 – Defining Equivalent Ratios
Define equivalent ratios and identify them in recipes, diagrams, and numerical examples. Explain how multiplying or dividing both quantities by the same factor creates an equivalent ratio.
Cool-down: Decide whether a pair of ratios is equivalent and support the answer with a diagram or calculation.

Thursday, November 5: Lesson 6 – Introducing Double Number Line Diagrams
Represent multiple batches and equivalent ratios on double number line diagrams. Interpret aligned values and connect each pair of values to the same ratio relationship.
Cool-down: Complete and interpret a double number line for a given ratio.

Friday, November 6: Lesson 7 – Creating Double Number Line Diagrams
Create, label, and use double number line diagrams to represent equivalent ratios and solve problems. Choose appropriate intervals and explain how corresponding values are related.
Cool-down: Construct a double number line and use it to answer an equivalent-ratio question.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath or lesson practice on equivalent ratios and double number line diagrams. Review and correct cool-down responses when requested. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will describe ratio relationships using the terms ratio, for every, batch, mixture, and equivalent.
Students will explain why two ratios are or are not equivalent using scaling language, diagrams, and numerical evidence.
Students will interpret and describe corresponding values on a double number line diagram using complete mathematical sentences.

objectives: Students will demonstrate their understanding of Unit 1 concepts on the delayed test and begin Unit 2 by exploring ratios. Students will compare two quantities, use ratio language accurately, and represent ratios with words, symbols, collections, and diagrams. A readiness check will help identify strengths and areas that need support before beginning the new unit.
agenda:
Monday, October 26: Unit 1 Test – Area, Surface Area, and Geometry
Complete the delayed Unit 1 test. Work independently, show calculations and reasoning, label answers with the correct units, and check each response before turning in the test.

Tuesday, October 27: Unit 2 Check Your Understanding
Complete a short readiness check for Unit 2: Introducing Ratios. Compare quantities, organize objects into categories, describe relationships between groups, and explain your thinking. This activity will show what we already understand and what we need to review.

Wednesday, October 28: Lesson 1 – Introducing Ratios and Ratio Language
Sort collections into categories and compare the amounts. Write ratio statements using words and symbols, including the words to and for every, as well as the colon notation a:b.

Thursday, October 29: Lesson 1 – Describing and Displaying Ratios
Describe the same collection with more than one correct ratio statement. Create a visual display that matches a ratio and explain how the display represents the relationship between two quantities.

Friday, October 30: Lesson 2 – Representing Ratios with Diagrams
Use diagrams to represent ratios. Match ratio statements to diagrams, create diagrams for given ratios, and explain how the groups in a diagram show the relationship between quantities.
homework: Prepare for Monday's Unit 1 test by reviewing class notes and corrected problems. After the test, complete any assigned DeltaMath or ratio practice. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to every class.
languageObjectives: Students will explain their Unit 1 test reasoning using accurate mathematical vocabulary and units.
Students will read, write, and say ratio statements using the phrases ratio of, to, and for every, as well as colon notation.
Students will describe how a collection or diagram represents a relationship between two quantities and compare equivalent descriptions of the same ratio.

objectives: Students will review and demonstrate their understanding of area, quadrilateral properties, polyhedra, nets, and surface area. They will choose appropriate formulas and strategies, identify corresponding bases and perpendicular heights, decompose figures, and account for every face of a solid. Students will explain their reasoning, correct errors, and use appropriate units as they prepare for Friday's test.
agenda:
Monday, October 19: Area and Quadrilateral Review
Review quadrilateral classifications and parallelogram side and angle relationships. Practice finding the areas of rectangles, parallelograms, and triangles using corresponding bases and perpendicular heights. Find polygon areas by decomposing, rearranging, or subtracting simpler shapes.

Tuesday, October 20: Polyhedra, Nets, and Surface Area Review
Identify prisms and pyramids and count their faces, edges, and vertices. Match solids to nets and calculate surface area by adding the areas of all faces, including hidden faces. Check that each face is counted exactly once.

Wednesday, October 21: Mixed Review and Test Preparation
Complete mixed practice covering the topics learned so far. Compare strategies, correct mistakes, and ask questions. Review the difference between surface area and volume, including square units versus cubic units. Identify which skills you need to practice before Friday's test.
Thursday, October 22: Field Trip to Fenway Park

Friday, October 23: Test – Area, Surface Area, and Geometry
Demonstrate your understanding of the topics reviewed this week. Work independently, show your calculations and reasoning, label answers with the correct units, and check your work.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath review practice. Study your class notes and corrected review problems for Friday's test, focusing on skills you still find challenging. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to every class.
languageObjectives: Students will explain and justify area strategies using the terms base, perpendicular height, decompose, and square units.
Students will describe quadrilateral properties and polyhedra using precise vocabulary, including parallel, congruent, supplementary, face, edge, vertex, prism, pyramid, and net.
Students will compare solutions, explain corrections, and distinguish surface area from volume using appropriate mathematical terms and units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will identify faces, edges, and vertices of polyhedra; connect solids to their nets; and calculate the surface area of prisms and pyramids by adding the areas of all faces. Students will explain their calculations and label answers in square units. If time allows, students will distinguish surface area from volume.
agenda: Monday, October 12: No School – Indigenous Peoples' Day

Tuesday, October 13: Lesson 13 Review and Lesson 14 – Nets and Surface Area
Review faces, edges, and vertices of prisms and pyramids. Match solids to their nets and explain how each face of a solid appears in its net.

Wednesday, October 14: Continue Lesson 14 – Nets and Surface Area
Use nets to organize surface-area calculations. Find the area of each face, include every face exactly once, and add the areas. Compare your method with a partner and label your answer in square units.

Thursday, October 15: Lesson 15 – More Nets, More Surface Area
Find the surface areas of prisms and pyramids using nets and labeled dimensions. Apply rectangle and triangle area formulas, identify corresponding bases and perpendicular heights, and justify your calculations.

Friday, October 16: Surface Area Practice and Review
Practice using nets, check for missing or double-counted faces, and explain your reasoning. If ready: Lesson 16 – Distinguishing Between Surface Area and Volume (Optional). Compare covering the outside of a solid with the space it occupies, using square units for surface area and cubic units for volume.
